**Elastic Compute Cloud** — Virtual servers in the cloud.

**Key facts**:
- Instance types: T (burstable), M (general), C (compute), R (memory), I (storage), P/G (GPU)
- Pricing: On-Demand, Reserved, Spot, Dedicated
- Storage: EBS (persistent), Instance Store (ephemeral)
- Placement Groups: Cluster (low latency), Spread (fault isolation), Partition (distributed databases)
- UserData: bootstrap script on first launch
- Metadata: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (instance info from within instance)

**Simple Storage Service** — Object storage, virtually unlimited.

**Key facts**:
- Max object size: 5 TB (multipart required >5 GB)
- 11 9s durability (99.999999999%)
- Bucket names are globally unique
- By default: private (block public access)
- Versioning: keeps all versions, protects against accidental delete
- Storage classes: Standard → IA → Glacier → Deep Archive
- Events: trigger Lambda/SQS/SNS on object operations
- Pre-signed URLs: temporary access without credentials

**Virtual Private Cloud** — Your isolated network in AWS.

**Components**:
- Subnets: public (has route to IGW) or private (no direct internet route)
- Internet Gateway (IGW): enables internet access for public subnet
- NAT Gateway: outbound-only internet for private subnets
- Route Tables: define where traffic goes
- Security Groups: stateful instance firewall (allow only)
- Network ACL: stateless subnet firewall (allow + deny)
- VPC Peering: connect two VPCs (non-transitive)
- Transit Gateway: hub for many VPCs + on-premises

**Identity and Access Management** — Control who can do what in AWS.

**Components**:
- Users: persons/apps with long-term credentials
- Groups: collection of users sharing policies
- Roles: temporary credentials for services/cross-account
- Policies: JSON documents defining permissions (Allow/Deny + Service + Action + Resource)
- Permission Boundaries: max permissions cap for a user/role
- Resource-based policies: attached to resources (S3, KMS, Lambda)

**Root user**: Unrestricted. Use only for account tasks. Always enable MFA.

**Relational Database Service** — Managed relational databases.

**Engines**: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, Amazon Aurora

**HA**: Multi-AZ = synchronous standby, auto-failover. No read traffic on standby.

**Scale reads**: Read Replicas (async, up to 5). Can be cross-Region.

**Backups**: Automated (1-35 days, point-in-time recovery). Manual snapshots (no expiry).

**Security**: Encryption at rest (KMS), in transit (SSL), VPC isolation, IAM auth for MySQL/PostgreSQL.

**Maintenance window**: Patching happens during your specified window.

**AWS-native relational database** (MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible).

**Performance**: 5x MySQL, 3x PostgreSQL throughput.

**Storage**: 6 copies across 3 AZs. Auto-grows in 10 GB increments up to 128 TB.

**Endpoints**:
- Cluster (writer) endpoint → always primary
- Reader endpoint → load balances read replicas
- Custom endpoint → subset of instances

**Aurora Global**: Primary + up to 5 secondary Regions. < 1 sec replication. Promote secondary in < 1 min for DR.

**Aurora Serverless v2**: Auto-scales capacity in fine-grained units. Great for variable workloads.

**Managed NoSQL** key-value and document database.

**Always remember**:
- Primary Key: Partition key (simple) or Partition + Sort key (composite)
- No fixed schema (except primary key)
- Single-digit ms latency at any scale
- 3 AZ replication by default
- DAX: microsecond read cache
- Streams: ordered change log (24-hr retention)
- Global Tables: multi-master, multi-region
- On-demand capacity: pay per request (no pre-planning)
- Provisioned capacity: specify RCU/WCU (cheaper at steady load)
- GSI: different partition key. LSI: same partition key, different sort key.

**Serverless compute** — Run code without managing servers.

**Key limits**:
- Max execution: 15 minutes
- Max memory: 10 GB (CPU scales proportionally)
- Concurrency: 1,000 per Region (default)
- Package size: 50 MB (ZIP) / 250 MB (unzipped) / 10 GB (container)

**Pricing**: Pay per invocation + duration (GB-seconds). 1M free requests/month.

**Cold start**: First invocation after idle. Use Provisioned Concurrency to eliminate.

**Execution role**: IAM role Lambda assumes to call AWS services.

**Triggers**: API Gateway, ALB, SQS, SNS, EventBridge, S3 events, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis.

**Content Delivery Network (CDN)** — Caches content at 400+ edge locations worldwide.

**Key features**:
- Reduces latency for static and dynamic content
- Origins: S3, ALB, EC2, HTTP endpoint
- TTL: controls how long content is cached
- Cache invalidation: force refresh cached content
- Geo-restriction: block/allow specific countries
- HTTPS: SSL/TLS termination at edge (ACM for free certs)
- WAF integration: Layer 7 protection at edge
- Lambda@Edge: run Lambda at edge locations
- Origin Access Control (OAC): restrict S3 to only CloudFront access

**Signed URLs/Cookies**: Time-limited access to protected content

**DNS service** — Translate domain names to IP addresses.

**Record types**:
- A: domain → IPv4
- AAAA: domain → IPv6
- CNAME: domain → domain (not for apex/root domain)
- Alias: AWS-specific, domain → AWS resource (free, works for apex)
- MX: mail server
- TXT: text verification

**Routing policies**: Simple, Weighted, Latency, Failover, Geolocation, Multi-Value

**Health checks**: Monitor endpoint health. Drive failover routing.

**Hosted zones**: Public (internet-facing) or Private (VPC-only).

**Domain registration**: Can register domains directly in Route 53.

**Key Management Service** — Create and control encryption keys.

**Key types**:
- AWS Managed Keys (aws/s3, aws/rds): auto-rotated yearly, free
- Customer Managed Keys (CMK): you control rotation, access, deletion. $1/month.
- Customer Provided Keys: imported, no AWS management

**Envelope encryption**: CMK encrypts a DEK (Data Encryption Key). DEK encrypts data. CMK never leaves KMS.

**Key policies**: Primary way to control key access (NOT just IAM).

**Audit**: All KMS API calls logged in CloudTrail.

**FIPS 140-2 Level 2**. For Level 3: use CloudHSM.

**Multi-Region Keys**: Primary in one Region, replicas in others.

**ECS (Elastic Container Service)**:
- AWS-native container orchestration
- Simpler, tighter AWS integration
- Launch types: EC2 (you manage instances) or Fargate (serverless)
- Task Definition: container blueprint (image, CPU, memory, ports, role)
- Service: maintains desired number of tasks
- Task Role: permissions for container. Execution Role: permissions to start container.

**EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service)**:
- Managed Kubernetes
- Industry standard, portable, vast ecosystem
- More complex to operate
- Node groups: EC2 nodes. Fargate profiles: serverless.

**Choose ECS**: When you want simpler AWS-native orchestration.
**Choose EKS**: When you need Kubernetes compatibility or have K8s expertise.

**Simple Queue Service** — Fully managed message queue.

**Standard Queue**: Best-effort ordering, at-least-once delivery, unlimited throughput.

**FIFO Queue**: Exact ordering, exactly-once processing, 3,000 msg/sec max. Name ends in `.fifo`.

**Key concepts**:
- Visibility Timeout (default 30s): hides message while being processed
- Long Polling: reduce empty responses, waits up to 20s for a message
- Dead Letter Queue (DLQ): for messages that fail processing N times
- Message retention: 1 minute to 14 days (default 4 days)
- Max message size: 256 KB

**Use with**: Lambda (trigger), EC2/ECS (consumers), SNS fan-out

**Simple Notification Service** — Pub/Sub messaging.

**How it works**:
- Publisher → Topic → Subscribers
- One message → delivered to ALL subscribers simultaneously

**Subscriber types**: SQS queue, Lambda, HTTP/HTTPS endpoint, email, SMS, mobile push

**Fan-out pattern**: SNS → multiple SQS queues. Decoupled, guaranteed delivery to each.

**FIFO Topics**: Ordered delivery to FIFO SQS queues only.

**Message filtering**: Subscribers can filter which messages they receive based on message attributes.

**SNS vs SQS**: SNS = push to many subscribers. SQS = queue for one consumer group to pull from.

**Monitoring and observability** service.

**Metrics**: Numeric time-series data from AWS services. EC2: CPU, network, disk. Custom metrics: your own.

**Alarms**: Trigger on metric threshold. Actions: SNS notification, EC2 action (stop/reboot/terminate), Auto Scaling.

**Logs**: Collect, monitor, and store log files. Log groups → log streams.

**Logs Insights**: Query log data with SQL-like syntax.

**Dashboards**: Visualize metrics from multiple services.

**Events/EventBridge**: Respond to state changes in AWS resources.

**Container Insights**: ECS/EKS cluster and container metrics.

**Default EC2 metrics**: CPU, network, disk. RAM requires CloudWatch agent (custom metric).

**Infrastructure as Code (IaC)** — Provision AWS resources from templates.

**Template**: JSON or YAML file describing resources (EC2, RDS, VPC, etc.).

**Stack**: A set of AWS resources created/managed as a unit from a template.

**Change Set**: Preview changes before applying them.

**Drift Detection**: Detect manual changes made outside CloudFormation.

**Nested Stacks**: Reference other stacks as resources (modular design).

**StackSets**: Deploy stacks across multiple accounts and Regions.

**Benefits**: Repeatable deployments, version control, rollback on failure.

**vs Terraform**: CloudFormation = AWS-only, always up-to-date. Terraform = multi-cloud, popular in practice.

**Platform as a Service (PaaS)** — Deploy web apps without managing infrastructure.

**What it does**: You upload your code → Beanstalk handles EC2, ELB, Auto Scaling, RDS, monitoring.

**Supports**: Java, .NET, PHP, Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, Docker.

**Deployment policies**:
- All at once: fast but downtime
- Rolling: gradual, reduced capacity during deploy
- Rolling with additional batch: no reduced capacity
- Immutable: new instances, safest, slowest
- Blue/Green: swap environments

**You control**: Environment configuration (instance type, scaling, env variables).

**Under the hood**: CloudFormation. Beanstalk is a UI/workflow on top.

**Fully managed API management** — Create, publish, maintain, monitor APIs.

**Types**:
- REST API: full features, caching, request/response transformation
- HTTP API: simpler, cheaper, lower latency (for Lambda and HTTP backends)
- WebSocket API: persistent connections for chat, real-time apps

**Integrations**: Lambda (serverless), HTTP backends, AWS services directly

**Features**:
- Authorization: IAM, Cognito, Lambda authorizer (custom)
- Throttling: 10,000 req/sec default per account
- Caching: reduce backend calls
- Stages: dev, staging, prod (separate environments)
- Usage plans and API keys: for external APIs with rate limiting

**CORS**: Must be enabled for browser clients calling cross-origin

**Threat detection** using ML.

**Data sources**:
- CloudTrail (API activity)
- VPC Flow Logs (network traffic)
- DNS logs (domain lookups)
- S3 data events (optional)
- EKS audit logs (optional)

**Findings examples**:
- UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/SSHBruteForce
- CryptoCurrency:EC2/BitcoinTool (crypto mining)
- Exfiltration:S3/ObjectRead.Unusual
- Trojan:EC2/DGADomainRequest

**Important**: GuardDuty is READ-ONLY. It doesn't block anything. Use EventBridge to trigger automated response (block IP via WAF, isolate instance via security group change).

**30-day free trial.** No agents required.

**Multi-account management** — Centrally manage AWS accounts.

**Structure**:
- Management (root) account: creates the org, pays consolidated bill
- Member accounts: workload accounts
- Organizational Units (OUs): group accounts (e.g., Sandbox OU, Production OU)

**Service Control Policies (SCPs)**:
- Applied to OUs or accounts
- Set MAXIMUM permissions (can't grant — only restrict)
- Apply to all principals except management account

**Benefits**:
- Consolidated billing (volume discounts, RI sharing)
- Centralized governance (SCPs)
- CloudTrail, Config, GuardDuty across all accounts
- AWS SSO/Identity Center for single sign-on

**Best practice**: Separate accounts for production, staging, dev, security, logging.

**Managed in-memory cache** — Redis or Memcached.

**Redis**:
- Sorted sets, lists, pub/sub, persistence, replication
- Multi-AZ with automatic failover
- Cluster mode: shard data across multiple nodes
- Use for: session store, leaderboards, real-time, pub/sub

**Memcached**:
- Simple, multi-threaded, no persistence
- Use for: simple cache, horizontal scaling

**Cache patterns**:
- Cache-aside (lazy loading): check cache, if miss → DB → cache
- Write-through: write to DB → update cache
- Write-behind: write to cache → async DB write

**TTL**: Set expiration on cache entries to prevent stale data.

**Session affinity alternative**: Store sessions in ElastiCache (enables any instance to serve any user).

**Dedicated network connection** from on-premises to AWS.

**Key facts**:
- Private fiber connection (NOT over public internet)
- Lower latency, consistent throughput vs VPN
- Bandwidth: 1 Gbps, 10 Gbps, 100 Gbps dedicated. 50–500 Mbps hosted (via partner).
- Setup time: weeks to months

**CRITICAL**: Direct Connect is **NOT encrypted by default**. Add Site-to-Site VPN over Direct Connect for encryption.

**High availability**: For critical workloads, use 2 Direct Connect connections OR Direct Connect + VPN backup.

**Direct Connect Gateway**: Connect to multiple VPCs across Regions from one Direct Connect connection.

**Use when**: Consistent high bandwidth, compliance requiring private path, or cost savings at scale.

**Secrets management** — Store, rotate, and retrieve secrets.

**Key features**:
- Automatic rotation: built-in support for RDS, DocumentDB, Redshift. Custom Lambda for others.
- Encryption: all secrets encrypted with KMS
- Versioning: old versions accessible during rotation
- Fine-grained access: IAM policies control who can retrieve which secrets
- Cross-account access: via resource-based policy

**vs SSM Parameter Store**:
- Secrets Manager: auto-rotation, $0.40/secret/month
- Parameter Store SecureString: no auto-rotation, free (standard tier)

**SDK pattern**: Call Secrets Manager API from app code to retrieve secret at runtime (not in environment variables or config files).

**Real-time data streaming** — Collect and process streaming data.

**Key concepts**:
- **Shard**: unit of capacity (1 MB/s write, 2 MB/s read, 1,000 PUT records/s)
- **Records**: sequence number + partition key + data blob (up to 1 MB)
- **Retention**: 24 hours to 365 days
- **Replay**: consumers can re-read data within retention window

**Consumers**:
- Standard (pull): 2 MB/s shared across all consumers per shard
- Enhanced fan-out: 2 MB/s per consumer per shard, push-based (better for multiple consumers)

**vs Firehose**: Streams = custom consumers, replay. Firehose = managed delivery to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch.

**vs SQS**: Kinesis = multiple consumers read same data. SQS = one consumer group per queue.

**API activity logging** — Track who did what, when, where.

**Records**: All API calls made via Console, CLI, SDK, or other AWS services.

**Event types**:
- Management events (control plane): create/delete/modify resources. Logged by default.
- Data events (data plane): S3 object reads/writes, Lambda invocations. Not logged by default (extra cost).
- Insights events: detect unusual API call patterns.

**Trail**: Configuration to deliver events to S3 and/or CloudWatch Logs.

**Retention**: Default 90 days in CloudTrail event history. Enable trail to store indefinitely in S3.

**Multi-region**: Enable trail in all Regions to capture global activity.

**Integrity**: Validate log files haven't been tampered with using CloudTrail log file validation.

**Configuration compliance** — Track resource configurations and compliance.

**What it does**:
- Continuously records resource configurations
- Detects configuration changes
- Evaluates against compliance rules

**Config Rules**: evaluate resources against desired configuration
- AWS Managed rules: pre-built (100+). e.g., `s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled`
- Custom rules: Lambda functions for custom logic

**Remediation**: Auto-remediate non-compliant resources via SSM Automation

**Conformance Packs**: collection of rules + remediation actions deployed as a unit (e.g., HIPAA, PCI-DSS packs)

**vs CloudTrail**: Config = 'what is the state?' CloudTrail = 'who changed it?'

**Load Balancing** — Distribute traffic across multiple targets.

**ALB (Application Load Balancer)** — Layer 7:
- Path routing: /api → backend, /static → S3
- Host routing: api.example.com vs www.example.com
- Targets: EC2, ECS tasks, Lambda, IP addresses

**NLB (Network Load Balancer)** — Layer 4:
- Ultra-low latency, millions of requests/sec
- Static Elastic IPs (one per AZ)
- Best for: non-HTTP, gaming, VoIP

**GWLB (Gateway Load Balancer)** — Layer 3:
- For virtual appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS)

**Common features**: Health checks, cross-AZ load balancing, access logs, SSL termination, sticky sessions (ALB/NLB)

**Serverless workflow orchestration** — Coordinate multi-step distributed applications.

**State types**:
- Task: invoke Lambda, ECS, SNS, SQS, Glue, etc.
- Choice: conditional branching
- Wait: pause for time or event
- Parallel: run branches concurrently
- Map: iterate over array

**Workflow types**:
- Standard: 1 year max, exactly-once, full audit history
- Express: 5 min max, at-least-once, high throughput

**WaitForTaskToken**: Pass a token to external system; workflow pauses until the token is sent back (for human approval, async tasks).

**Use for**: Order processing, data pipelines, ETL workflows, microservice orchestration, approval flows

**Serverless SQL on S3** — Query data in S3 without loading it into a database.

**Key facts**:
- Presto-based, standard SQL
- Pay per query: **$5 per TB scanned**
- Supports: CSV, JSON, Parquet, ORC, Avro, TSV
- Works with AWS Glue Data Catalog for schema management

**Cost optimization**:
- Use columnar formats (Parquet/ORC): scan only needed columns → 30-90% cost reduction
- Partition data: scan only relevant partitions
- Compress data: less data to scan

**Best for**: Ad-hoc queries, log analysis, one-off exploration, serverless BI

**Not for**: High-frequency queries needing ms response (use Redshift or ElastiCache), transactional data (use RDS/DynamoDB)

**Managed file transfer** using standard protocols.

**Supported protocols**:
- SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol)
- FTPS (FTP over SSL/TLS)
- FTP
- AS2

**Destinations**: Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS

**Use case**: Business partners, customers, or legacy systems that require SFTP/FTP to exchange files. Replaces on-premises SFTP servers.

**Authentication**: Service-managed (built-in user directory), Microsoft AD, custom Lambda authorizer

**Key benefit**: Drop-in replacement for SFTP servers. Partners use the same SFTP tools/workflow, but data lands in S3.

**vs DataSync**: Transfer Family = SFTP/FTP protocol support. DataSync = agent-based accelerated transfers.
